attempts.label: DANDI:002035
attempts.paper_title: Amyloid Pathology in the Central Auditory Pathway of 5XFAD Mice Appears First in Auditory Cortex
attempts.entry_title: Amyloid pathology in the central auditory pathway of 5XFAD mice (Weible and Wehr 2022)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, so none is confirmed or contradicted. These are the onset of intracellular Abeta42 in layer 5 of auditory cortex by p21, before the MGB and inferior colliculus, the later spread of plaques, earlier pathology in the subiculum, and no label in the lateral lemniscus or cochlear nuclei. The dataset records the brain region for only 864 of its 12394 images, with no section positions or atlas alignment, so no per-region count can be formed. The hand counts, boundaries and areas behind the figures are not deposited, and the wild-type controls were not imaged. The few region-labelled images were not scored, as their scale is unverified.
attempts.description: Checks dandiset 002035 against the findings of Weible and Wehr (2022) on the onset and spread of Abeta42 label in the central auditory pathway of 5XFAD mice. The dandiset holds the raw widefield images of 62 5XFAD mice, but the region of 93% of the images is not recorded and no image carries a position, so no per-region count can be formed and every claim is blocked. The notebook checks the subjects, the files and the stated image scales, shows the region coverage, tests whether fields can be placed in their overviews, and shows the region-labelled Abeta42 images.

notebooks.title: Testing Weible and Wehr (2022) on dandiset 002035

outcomes.statement: In 5XFAD mice amyloid pathology in the central auditory pathway appears first in A1, as intracellular Abeta42 in layer 5 neurons by p21, before any label in MGB, IC, SOC, nLL or CN.
outcomes.source: Results, Primary auditory cortex, paragraph 1; Discussion, paragraph 1; Figure 1A
outcomes.quote: Amyloid pathology in the central auditory pathway of Aβ42+ mice appeared first in A1
outcomes.notes: Needs the first age with Abeta42 label in each of A1, MGB, IC, SOC, nLL and CN. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage). The region coverage by age is A1 2 mice, MGB 3, IC 3, SOC 5, CN 2, nLL none, so the onset age of no region can be read. The README's rule that a region without images had no label judged present cannot be applied when the region of most images is unknown. No 200X Abeta42 image is labelled A1 (its 9 labelled images are DAPI), so no age of A1 label can be read even in the labelled rounds. Fields can be placed in their 12.5X overviews for 26 of 66 sampled fields, but no overview is aligned to the atlas (notebook, cells tagged placement).

The subiculum is labelled in follow-up subfolders of 17 mice, one of the 5 p14 mice (NN); the subiculum images of the main pass of the other mice are not labelled, so neither 'every p14 mouse' nor the first age with plaques can be read. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage). The 200X Abeta42 subiculum images of the 5 p60 mice and of the 8 younger mice (NN, 0324, 0334, 0294, 0214, 0219, 0241, 0248) were listed and shown (notebook, cells tagged labelled), but not scored. Their scale is not verified (554 of the 561 region-labelled 200X Abeta42 images are classed 200X by rule), an intensity count cannot tell cells from plaques or from autofluorescence, and the paper's identification by eye against wild-type sections cannot be repeated without those sections. Fields chosen within the subiculum cannot show that plaques are absent before p60.

outcomes.statement: There are no Abeta42+ cells or plaques in the nucleus of the lateral lemniscus or the cochlear nuclei through p150.
outcomes.source: Results, Superior olivary complex, nucleus of the lateral lemniscus, and cochlear nuclei, paragraph 1; Figure 6C and 6D
outcomes.quote: We saw no evidence of Aβ42+ cells or plaques in either the nLL or the CN (Fig. 6C, D)
outcomes.notes: Needs counts in the nLL and the cochlear nuclei of every mouse. The nLL is never labelled; the CN is labelled in 2 mice ('0136 follow-up CN', and '0215 follow-up IC, VCN', which mixes IC and VCN). The README says a region without images had no label judged present, but the region of most images is unknown, so absence cannot be read from the file list. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage). The 7 CN-labelled 200X Abeta42 images of mouse 0136 and the 23 IC;VCN images of mouse 0215 were listed and shown (notebook, cells tagged labelled). The CN field of 0136 placed in its overview has at least twice the stated pixel size and covers the whole ventral cochlear nucleus. The 0136 CN subfolder holds Abeta42 and DAPI images only, so its bright puncta have no red-channel reference, and an intensity count cannot class them as cells, plaques or autofluorescence. The 0215 IC and VCN subfolder holds 6 red-channel images; 4 follow an Abeta42 field (2 at 100X, 2 at 200X). In these 4 pairs the log images of the two channels correlate at 0.987 to 0.995, and all 22 objects found in the Abeta42 images are also at least 7 scaled MADs above background in the red image (notebook, cells tagged labelled). Whether these fields lie in the IC or the VCN is not recorded, they are 4 fields and not the whole nucleus, and the paper's identification by eye against wild-type sections cannot be repeated. The images were not scored, so the claim was neither confirmed nor refuted on them.

outcomes.statement: Intracellular Abeta42 appears in the PRNc, in putative giant reticulospinal neurons and smaller cells, as early as p14 and consistently by p21; the overall Abeta42+ cell density (below 2%) varies with age, with a trend for the RSNs alone.
outcomes.source: Results, Caudal pontine reticular nucleus, paragraph 1; Figure 7B; Table 6
outcomes.quote: We observed intracellular Aβ42 both in putative giant RSNs and other smaller cells in the PRNc as early as p14, and consistently by p21 (Fig. 7B) ... The density of the overall Aβ42+ cell population varied with age, with a trend also seen specifically for RSNs (Fig. 7B, Table 6)
outcomes.notes: Needs, per mouse with a PRNc section (about 38), Abeta42+ cells and DAPI cells in an 800 um circle in ventrolateral PRNc, and cell diameters. PRNc is labelled in 10 mice (3 at p14, 3 at p21, 3 at p30, 1 at p150), so the Kruskal-Wallis across ages cannot be run, and the p14 and p21 parts would rest on 3 mice each with no boundary for the ventrolateral PRNc. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage). The 25 PRNc 200X Abeta42 images of the p14 mice BrTNR, LTN and NN were listed and shown (notebook, cells tagged labelled). Their fields placed in the overviews have 8 times (BrTNR, LTN) and 4 times (NN) the stated 0.3225 um pixel size against a 12.5X overview. With the overview between 12.5X and 50X (Methods, Imaging) the BrTNR and LTN fields have between 0.645 and 2.58 um per pixel, and possibly more, since 2.58 um is the largest size tried. Pixels of that size would resolve a 40 um cell, but with the scale known only within a factor of 4 a diameter cannot be read in micrometres, so the >40 um condition cannot be tested; and cells cannot be told from autofluorescence without the wild-type reference. The p14 condition was not tested.

outcomes.statement: Plaques in the PRNc first appear at p90 and vary in density with age.
outcomes.source: Results, Caudal pontine reticular nucleus, paragraph 1; Figure 7C; Table 6
outcomes.quote: Plaques, first evident at p90, also varied in density with age (Fig. 7C, Table 6)
outcomes.notes: Needs per-mouse PRNc plaque density at every age; PRNc is labelled in 10 mice, one of them older than p30, so the onset at p90 and the age test cannot be read. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage).

outcomes.statement: PRNc pathology shows no sex differences.
outcomes.source: Results, Caudal pontine reticular nucleus, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: No sex-linked differences were observed
outcomes.notes: Needs the per-mouse PRNc measures of fig7b-prnc-cells and fig7c-prnc-plaques, which cannot be formed. Only 864 of 12394 images (7.0%) have a recorded region, all from named follow-up subfolders in 24 of the 62 mice, and none of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate (notebook, cell tagged coverage).

outcomes.statement: In A1, subiculum and IC, Abeta42+ cells are first seen about 2 months before plaques.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In cortex, subiculum, and inferior colliculus, Aβ42+ cells were first observed roughly 2 months prior to the appearance of plaques
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig1a-a1-onset-p21, fig3a-subiculum-onset, ic-cells-low, fig2b-a1-plaques-age and fig5b-ic-plaques-age, all blocked as metadata_insufficient.

outcomes.statement: At least 24% of L5A and 11% of L5B pyramidal neurons in A1 are Abeta42+ at 5 months of age, an estimate from the Abeta42+ cell densities and the prevalence of pyramidal neurons in L5.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Based on the prevalence of pyramidal ... neurons in L5 [30], we estimate that at least 24% of L5A (and 11% of L5B) pyramidal neurons are Aβ42+ at 5 months of age
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig1e-l5a-peak, blocked as metadata_insufficient. The outside input (the Blue Brain cell atlas, Ero et al. 2018) was therefore not fetched or pinned.

findings.statement: The imaged region is recorded for 864 of the 12394 images (7.0%), and for 561 of the 7048 200X Abeta42 images, only where an original follow-up subfolder named it; 38 of the 62 mice have no region on any image, and the nucleus of the lateral lemniscus is never named. None of 20 sampled image headers and sidecars holds a stage position, section number or atlas coordinate, and samples.json says individual sections are not tracked. Fields can be matched to the low-magnification overviews before them for 26 of 66 sampled fields, but no overview is aligned to an atlas. The images of the main imaging pass cannot be assigned to a region, an A1 layer or a subdivision, so none of the paper's per-region values can be formed from the dandiset.

The dandiset holds the raw images only: none of the cell and plaque markings, region and laminar boundaries, CCFv3 alignments, region areas or DAPI counts on which every figure and table of the paper rests.
The 25 wild-type control mice of the paper are not in the dandiset; its README says they showed no detectable label and were not imaged. The paper's control claim cannot be tested.

The dandiset has 62 5XFAD mice, against the paper's 61: p120 has 9 mice (5 females, 4 males) and p45 has 3 females and 5 males, where the paper gives 4 males and 4 females at every age from p21 to p150. In all 30 females and 32 males. Sex, age and subject label agree with the original folder names for every mouse.
The Methods (Mice) give 61 5XFAD mice as '31 females and 30 males', but the per-age numbers they give (4 and 4 from p21 to p150, 2 females and 3 males at p14) add up to 30 females and 31 males.

Magnification is not recorded reliably by the acquisition software; the dandiset infers it from image content, and assigns 7125 Abeta42 and red-channel images to 200X by rule. On a seeded sample, DAPI nuclei measure about the same median diameter in the 100X and 200X classes (4.2 and 5.1 um from .czi files) and a 100X field holds 3.6 times as many, consistent with the stated ratio of the two classes.

The magnification classes do not agree with the overviews. Of 66 sampled fields matched by cross-correlation to the 12.5X overviews of their block, 26 are placed, and none at its stated pixel size: against an overview at 5.16 um the best field pixel size is 2 times the stated one for 17 of the 26, 4 times for 6 and 8 times for 3. With the overviews between 12.5X and 50X, as the paper says of its low-magnification images, 3 images classed 200X by rule (the cochlear nucleus field of mouse 0136, the PRNc fields of the p14 mice BrTNR and LTN) have at least 0.645 um per pixel, twice the stated 0.3225 um; these three are best at 2.58 um, the largest size tried, so their true ratio may be higher than 8. Either the overview or the field class is wrong for the others. The pixel sizes of the sidecars and OME headers cannot be relied on for measurements in micrometres.

entries.name: weible-2022
entries.title: Amyloid pathology in the central auditory pathway of 5XFAD mice (Weible and Wehr 2022)
entries.description: Checks dandiset 002035 against the findings of Weible and Wehr (2022) on the onset and spread of Abeta42 label in the central auditory pathway of 5XFAD mice. The dandiset holds the raw widefield images of 62 5XFAD mice, but the region of 93% of the images is not recorded and no image carries a position, so no per-region count can be formed and every claim is blocked. The notebook checks the subjects, the files and the stated image scales, shows the region coverage, tests whether fields can be placed in their overviews, and shows the region-labelled Abeta42 images.

notebooks.title: Testing Weible and Wehr (2022) on dandiset 002035
